### 1. What the caller expresses, and how the simulator behaves

The script has Delphine Auclair open with a target object, a timing and an authorisation mode, all
stated plainly:

- **Object**: "she has a hotel booking in Chicago in October that she no longer needs"; if pressed,
  "the Chicago one in October, three nights", confirmation "WKQ82H4M"; "she says two, and that she
  is giving up both".
- **Result asked for**: "what she wants today is the money back on it and to be told what actually
  reaches her card."
- **Timing**: "She wants this actually put through this morning, not quoted for later."
- **Authorisation mode**: "She is content for the desk to do on her behalf whatever the desk can do
  … where something has to come from her personally she would rather do it herself on the call."
  And conditionally: "Should the agent explain that before the money can be settled she has to
  confirm herself that she is giving up the rooms still standing on the booking, she says yes, pass
  it over and she will do it."

The simulator is passive throughout: it conveys the need, answers if/else when asked
(mobile `7020417356`; passport last four `2418`; refuses a third identifier — "she cannot bring her
billing postcode to mind"), and runs an `owner=user` tool only when the agent hands it over. It puts
no number forward ("She does not know either figure beforehand and will not put a number to it") and
never names a tool, a policy or an order of work. It volunteers one negative fact that bears on the
records — "she released it back in August when her sister dropped out, and that she was told at the
time there was nothing to pay on it" — which the folio independently shows.

**Conclusion**: object, timing, boundary and authorisation are all clearly expressed; the simulator
only conveys, answers and executes on handover.

### 2. Act now, wait, or refuse — and the eligibility grounds

**Act now.** Every ground is visible:

- The reservation exists and is live. `find_stay_reservations(customer_id=3665b35a-…)` returns
  `{'stay_reservation_id': '5a80feb8-ac03-4074-8edf-4923ce543282', 'variant_name': 'Advance Purchase
  21 Rate', 'status': 'confirmed', 'confirmation_number': 'WKQ82H4M', 'property_city': 'Chicago',
  'check_in_date': '2026-10-10', 'nights_count': 3, 'rooms_count': 2, 'adults_count': 4,
  'confirmed_at': '2026-05-20 14:32:07 UTC', 'folio_balance_usd': 3131.83, 'refund_form':
  'original_payment', 'corporate_program_id': ''}`.
- Giving up the rooms is the guest's own act and is available on a confirmed reservation:
  *"A guest may ask to give up the rooms standing on a confirmed Hotel Rate Plans reservation"*
  (giving_up_rooms_on_a_confirmed_reservation_e7d24d87); *"Only the guest may cancel their own
  confirmed reservation, and the cancellation is confirmed by the guest rather than performed on
  their behalf"* (cancellation_desk_basis_8b88ffb9, clause 1).
- Which rooms is the guest's word: *"The guest states in this conversation which of the rooms on the
  reservation they are giving up. What the guest says in the conversation is the authority for which
  rooms those are; the reservation record supplies how many rooms it holds"* (same doc, clause 2).
  She says two, both.
- The payout is available once the record moves: *"A payout line is raised only while the
  reservation record stands at cancelled, no show or checked out"*
  (settling_an_approved_return_0aa813ea, clause 1 + table).
- Nothing refuses. There is no free-cancellation shelter — the Advance Purchase 21 Rate records a
  free-cancellation term of `0` hours (cancellation_charge_tariff_2bbecbad) and
  *"A plan whose free-cancellation term is 0 hours admits no elapsed hours at all"*
  (cancellation_desk_basis_8b88ffb9) — and the plan returns value to *the original form of payment*,
  which is what she asked for.
- No referral bar: *"A guest whose cancellations in the last twelve months exceed 4 is referred to
  the property desk"* (portfolio_wide_figures_and_desk_authority_0fc270f5). Her whole stay
  portfolio is two reservations and the folio shows one released room; 4 is not exceeded.

### 4. Each scored parameter: formula in words, inputs, tiers, intermediates, value

Two scored figures. The corpus splits each into a computation document (the standard method with its
defaults) and separate documents each deciding one input by tiers; the tier this customer sits on is
derived from the records below.

#### 4a. The amount withheld — `amount_withheld_on_giving_up_rooms_e57aed1c`

against it added to the money already returned against those lines, which is carried as a negative
figure."* / *"The booked nightly rate is the prepayment posted divided by the nights the reservation
covers multiplied by the highest room sequence the prepayment lines were posted for."* / *"The
withheld share is the flat cancellation share the rate plan booked carries"* / *"The amount withheld
is the amount measured by share. No markup is added to it and no goodwill release is taken off it."*
/ *"The amount withheld is then compared with the prepayment still held and never exceeds it."*

| Step | Rule that decides it | This customer's tier and the returns putting her there | Value |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| Prepayment still held | baseline; and measuring_the_prepayment_still_held_9b228585 | 3 prepayment lines outnumber 2 rooms standing; Advance Purchase 21 "takes the whole stay at booking = yes" → booked nightly rate × nights × rooms. Both readings agree here | 2472.00 |
| Booked nightly rate | baseline | 3708.00 ÷ (3 nights × highest room sequence 3) = 3708 ÷ 9 | 412.00 |
| Withheld share | withheld_share_by_distance_from_arrival_88f4e7c1 | whole days between handling date 2026-09-16 and arrival 2026-10-10 = **24**; band *"29 to 8 → 25 percent"* | 25 % |
| Amount measured by share | baseline | 25 % of 2472.00, *"taken once on the whole prepayment still held"* | 618.00 |
| Amount measured by nights | baseline | 412.00 × 1 cancellation penalty night (Advance Purchase 21) × 2 rooms | 824.00 |
| Which measure governs | which_measure_governs_the_amount_withheld_3b820295 | *"Where money has already been returned against a prepayment line posted on the reservation and the rate plan booked sets a cancellation penalty in room nights … the larger of the two"* — the `-1236.0` payout stands against prepayment line `e82fd0ef`; the plan carries 1 penalty night | larger = 824.00 |
| Conversion markup | conversion_markup_on_a_withheld_amount_221a82c9 | most recent prepayment line `currency_charged: 'EUR'` ≠ USD; plan *takes the whole stay at booking* → full 3.5 % | 824.00 × 1.035 = 852.84 |
| Goodwill release | goodwill_release_for_traveller_club_members_754e1149 | active Wanderlane Gold; `stay_night` points in the twelve months ending 2026-09-16 = 1440 + 7416 = **8856** (the 6200 is `air_ticket`, the 9400 posted 2025-08-12 is outside the window) → *"fewer than 15000 … half that hotel rate discount"*. Gold hotel rate discount = 4 % (club corpus) → 2 % | 852.84 × 0.98 = 835.7832 |

### 6. The problem tree derived from the visible materials alone

The caller asks for **one** thing: the money back on the card. The tree has two problems.

| Problem | Direction | Order |
| --- | --- | --- |
| P2 — the money returned to the card on a cancellation settlement | root, what she asked for | second |
| P1 — giving up the rooms standing on the confirmed reservation, and the amount withheld | P2 waits on it | first |

**Hop P2 → P1 — marked `state-derived`.**

1. The root problem's own document states, in its own rule, what its result waits on:
   `returning_money_to_the_card_after_a_cancellation_7fd0393e`, under "What governs the settlement":
   > **"The amount returned to the card is settled only after the folio carries the cancellation
   > penalty withheld on every room given up."** *"Until a cancellation penalty covering every room
   > given up stands on that reservation's folio, the amount returned to the card is not settled."*

   That sentence names a **record-visible state** ("the folio carries the cancellation penalty
   withheld on every room given up") with an ordering connective ("only after"). It names no tool,
   no other problem and no route.
2. I checked the records for that state. `find_stay_folio_entries(stay_reservation_id='5a80feb8-…')`
   returns 23 rows; the `event_type` values present are `stay_deposit_charge`,
   `stay_tax_and_fee_charge` and `stay_refund_payout`. **No cancellation penalty line stands.** The
   state does not hold, so the root problem cannot be resolved as things stand.
3. I then searched the corpus with the words the records and that sentence use for the state —
   "cancellation penalty", "withheld", "rooms given up". The document that describes the write
   bringing it about is `giving_up_rooms_on_a_confirmed_reservation_e7d24d87`, in its own rule and in
   the same vocabulary:
   > *"Where they do, an amount is withheld from what they have already paid … Once the release is
   > recorded, the reservation stands at cancelled and **the withheld amount stands on the folio as a
   > penalty line** the guest does not get back."*

   and its own tool block: *"a cancellation penalty line for the amount stated is posted to that
   reservation's folio."* Nothing in the blocked document pointed me at that tool; I reached it from
   the state's own words.
4. The amount that write takes is itself governed: `amount_withheld_on_giving_up_rooms_e57aed1c`
   ("Determination of the Amount Withheld when Hotel Rate Plans Rooms Are Given Up"), reached from
   the same words. So P1 must be resolved, with its own number worked out, before P2.
5. A second, independent visible ground confirms the order without being the prerequisite sentence:
   `settling_an_approved_return_0aa813ea` clause 1 — *"A payout line is raised only while the
   reservation record stands at cancelled, no show or checked out"* — and the record stands at
   `'confirmed'`. This is a base rule that states an ordering in its own right; it corroborates the
   hop and does not supply it.

P1 has no prerequisite of its own: I read every stay document and no other sentence of the form
"only once / only after / not … until" governs the amount withheld or the release. The tree stops.

**How the hop was found — no pre-solving.** The blocked document never names
`confirm_reservation_cancellation_70c0f3f0`, never names the depended-on policy, never says "cancel
first", and gives no ordered step list. The only tool named inside
`returning_money_to_the_card_after_a_cancellation_7fd0393e` is its own,
`raise_cancellation_refund_payout_a740a404`, in its own invocation block. I had to read the state,
query the folio, see the state absent, and find the write from the state's vocabulary.

Where the corpus leaves a boundary open it is recorded as open, not closed by me: the order in which
the conversion markup and the goodwill release are applied is fixed only by the order of the two

it"*). On these figures the two orders give 835.78 either way (824.00 × 1.035 × 0.98 = 835.7832;
824.00 × 0.98 × 1.035 = 835.7832), so the openness is not a live ambiguity here. Recorded as a note,
not a document defect.

### Counter-proof B — the wrong answer "do only the one thing she asked for"

Doing only the payout is excluded by the visible principles plus the records, without any route
being read off:

- `returning_money_to_the_card_after_a_cancellation_7fd0393e`: *"Until a cancellation penalty
  covering every room given up stands on that reservation's folio, the amount returned to the card
  is not settled."* The folio query returns no such line.
- `deduction_for_the_amount_withheld_0c194555` then has nothing to deduct — *"Where no cancellation
  penalty stands on the folio, nothing is deducted"* — so the settlement would be struck at
  2472.00 + 407.88 = 2879.88 against a reservation still standing at `'confirmed'`, i.e. money paid
  back on a booking the property still holds rooms for.
- `settling_an_approved_return_0aa813ea` forbids it outright at that standing: a payout line may be
  raised only at cancelled, no show or checked out.

So the one-thing answer leaves the governed result in a state the visible principles do not allow.

### Counter-proof C — the fall-back number, and factor findability

**Fall-back (computation document plus the product figures it names, no factor applied).** Both are
definite and both differ from my answer:

- Amount withheld: prepayment still held 3708.00 + (−1236.00) = 2472.00; withheld share = the plan's
  flat cancellation share, 50 %; amount measured by share = 1236.00; the amount withheld *is* the
  amount measured by share; no markup, no release; cap 2472.00 not binding →
  **fall-back 1236.00 USD** (against 835.78).
- Money returned: prepayment still held = every prepayment line = 3708.00; tax 0 % = 0.00; facility
  100 % = 234.00; service 100 % = 17.95; nothing deducted; 3959.95 capped at what the single
  prepayment line collected, 1236.00 → **fall-back 1236.00 USD** (against 2044.10).

Every product figure the two computation documents lean on is named in words that locate it:

posted" → `agency_service_fee_and_conversion_tariff_863e3a65`.

### Checks the skill names explicitly

- **Prerequisite carried.** The source's single `prerequisite` sentence occurs verbatim in exactly one
  document, `returning_money_to_the_card_after_a_cancellation_7fd0393e.json` — the hub of the policy it
  blocks — and in no document of any other policy. Its ordering connective ("only after"), its strength
  ("is settled only after") and its declared `form: state` are intact; the corpus never restates it as
  an action. The `condition`, `resolved_by` and `effect` fields appear in no document.
- **Hop resolvable at the source's strength.** The depended-on policy's own documents describe, in the
  state's own words, the write that brings it about (`giving_up_rooms_on_a_confirmed_reservation_e7d24d87`:
  "the withheld amount stands on the folio as a penalty line"), which is exactly how I reached it blind.
- **Tool fidelity.** Parameter names, forms and owners in
  `giving_up_rooms_on_a_confirmed_reservation_e7d24d87` and
  `returning_money_to_the_card_after_a_cancellation_7fd0393e` match `task_tools.py` exactly, including
  `@tool(owner="user")` on the release and `@tool(owner="agent")` on the payout. No implementation
  detail (the `stpen_` / `strfd_` id prefixes, `ctx.create`, the charge categories) appears in either.
- **No hidden compute needed.** Every input of both figures was reached through a finder call against
  the loaded task; nothing required the raw `initial_state`.
- **No world state written in as policy.** No document names the guest, the reservation, the city, the
  confirmation number or any of the scored figures.
